title: perf(local): one insert per datasource for OTLP exports that arrive together

summaries.body:
<!-- maple-pr-review 2085c347-dfad-4fc7-aca3-e01eac01ace3 0 -->
## Maple review

🟢 **Confidence 10/10** · safe to merge
Merging, per-export commit accounting and single-export failure isolation are each pinned by tests, including a real-chDB read-your-writes case; only the shutdown flush ordering has no test.
<sub>no findings · tests covered · risk medium</sub>

Replaces per-export chDB inserts with a batcher that merges exports arriving in one tick into a single insert per datasource, keeping per-export commit counts and failing only the export whose rows the engine refuses. Sound and safe to merge.

- `InsertBatcher` merges concurrent exports into one chDB insert per datasource
- `Chdb.beforeEachStatement` flushes queued rows ahead of every other statement, keeping read-your-writes
- A failed shared statement is retried per export, so one refused row fails only its owner
- `ingest` posts `InsertBatcher.insert` instead of inserting batch by batch

<details><summary>What was checked</summary>

- Lone export still costs one insert: empty and single-statement exports take the no-wait path (`apps/cli/src/server/insert-batcher.ts:88`, `apps/cli/test/insert-batcher.test.ts:114`)
- `buildInsertStatements` output is unchanged — it delegates to the new builder, and `apps/cli/test/inserts.test.ts:68` pins byte-identical SQL
- Failure accounting: `accepted` only counts statements actually committed, and later datasources of a failed export are skipped (`insert-batcher.ts:118`, `:144`, test `:48`/`:65`)

</details>
